summary: Somerset County, ME lookout: fire station built 1911, 48-foot steel tower erected 1914; FFLA lists it standing; trail page says the tower should be viewed, not climbed.

facts.design: 48-foot steel tower (1914), with a former fire warden cabin at the summit

staffing.status: fire detection system described as now abandoned; no current staffing found

access.note: Hiking trail open via a temporary parking area the landowner allows; the cabin and tower are best viewed and not entered (Maine Trail Finder)

visit.trail_note: Maine Trail Finder: trailhead not yet constructed; parking on the logging road south of the ridge is allowed by the landowner. The tower should not be climbed.

facts.agency: Maine Forestry District (per Forest Lookouts); trailhead and summit planned to pass to the Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

events.note: Fire station built on the mountain in the spring and in operation early that year; building, furnishings and telephone line totalled $183.34

A watchman located a fire near Brassua Pond on July 5 (lightning); a fire was noted on the west part of Misery near Cold Stream Pond on July 10 (a dropped match); both were put out at a cost of $150 to the state
Maine Forest Service published a 360-degree panoramic map centered on the tower

notes_for_editor: Standing status rests on the FFLA index (no asterisk) and the trail page's description of a fire tower at the summit; no recent photo or visit report was checked. Access level 'restricted' is a judgment: the trail is open by landowner permission and the tower is not to be entered. The trail page is undated apart from a 2019 review, so the 'trailhead not yet constructed' note may be out of date. The 1912 watchman is not named in the source. The 1911 fire station may be the cabin the trail page describes; the sources do not say so outright, so the story does not claim it. AllTrails returned 403 and was not used.
